question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)}{2}, & \,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2} \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{\pi }{4},\,\text{E}[Y]=\frac{\pi }{4},\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.4332,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.4332,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician and integration by parts, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}xy\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)}{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}xy\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[\frac{\pi }{2}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-y)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-y)-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(-y)]\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{\pi }{2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[(\frac{\pi }{2}-1)(y\operatorname{sin}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)+\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡y]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{\pi }{2}-1)\frac{\pi }{2}+1-(\frac{\pi }{2}-1)] \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}-4\pi +8}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}-4\pi +8}{8}-(\frac{\pi }{4})(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}-8\pi +16}{16} \\  & ={(\frac{\pi }{4}-1)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{{(\frac{\pi }{4}-1)}^{2}}{(0.4332)\cdot (0.4332)} \\  & ≈0.25,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
